observation.visible_scene: A white ceramic bowl resting on a wooden surface is filled with a glossy, viscous red liquid. On the left side of the liquid's surface there is a curved, scalloped (wavy-edged) band of slightly thicker/textured red material that arcs from the upper-left down toward the lower-center. A bright white specular reflection (the light source) sits near the bottom of the liquid pool. The red pool is surrounded by a thin lighter-red ring and a white gap to the bowl's rim.
visible_changes: Over the excerpt the scalloped band on the left gradually recedes leftward and shrinks in extent: its upper portion shortens and disappears first, and by the last frames only a short, thin scalloped remnant remains near the left mid-height, whereas at the start the band was a long, thick arc reaching well toward the center.
The main body of the red liquid, the lighter-red ring at the rim, and the bright white reflection spot stay in essentially the same positions and shapes throughout.

The bowl and background remain fixed in the frame, indicating little or no camera motion; the visible change is the slow leftward retraction/diminishing of the scalloped feature, not a translation of the whole scene.
outside_clip_unknowns: The physical identity of the scalloped band (a surface ripple, a dissolving/partially submerged object, or a poured edge) is not determinable from these frames.
Whether the retraction of the band began before t=0 or continues after t=2.667s is unknown.
No cause, operator, or impact is visible to explain the band's motion.
uncertain_details: Minor sub-pixel drift of the camera or bowl cannot be fully excluded, but no clear camera pan/zoom is supported.
Whether the left boundary of the red pool shifts slightly along with the band is ambiguous; the dominant visible change is the band's own leftward shrinkage.
The exact mechanism (absorption, sinking, wave collapse) producing the band's reduction is not observable.
